2026-12-01.title: First Tuesday of Annunciation
2026-12-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Now is the moment to wake from sleep
Zechariah did not believe the angel
2026-12-01.alt: The 25 Days' Fast traditionally begins today.
2026-12-01.verse: Because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time, you will become mute, unable to speak, until the day these things occur.
theo: Paul's call fits the beginning of the fast: “You know what time it is, how it is now the moment for you to wake from sleep. For salvation is nearer to us now than when we became believers; the night is far gone, the day is near. Let us then lay aside the works of darkness and put on the armour of light… put on the Lord Jesus Christ.”

Zechariah asks for a sign: “How will I know that this is so?” Gabriel's answer is both a rebuke and a gift: he will be silent until the promise is fulfilled. His nine months of silence become a retreat. During this fast, a little silence, from screens, gossip and noise, can prepare us to speak praise at Christmas.
outline: Salvation is near; put on the armour of light.
He asked for proof instead of trusting the word.
Silence can become a school of faith and praise.
live: Choose one daily silence for the 25 days: no phone for an hour, no TV at dinner.
Pay one “debt of love” today: a visit, a call, an apology.
2026-12-01.prayer: Lord, wake me from sleep and clothe me with your light. Forgive my doubts, and let the silence of these days prepare my heart to sing your praise. Amen.
altar: The Nombu leads to the Holy Qurbana of Christmas. Each Qurbana during these days is a step towards the manger: we listen to the promise in the readings and receive the One who is coming.

2026-12-01.question: What noise keeps me from hearing God?

family.explain: Paul tells us it is time to wake up, because Jesus is coming. We prepare for Christmas by putting away bad habits and putting on Jesus, like new clothes.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may keep the Christmas fast with joy and love.
family.ask: Ask: “What one thing will each of us give up, and what one good thing will we do, during this Nombu?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to wake from sleep and to put on your light. As we begin the Christmas fast, open our ears to your word and our hearts to your coming. Amen.
share: Paul says the night is far gone and the day is near (Romans 13:12). In what area of my life am I still half asleep?
Zechariah could not speak for nine months. What noise could I give up this Nombu to listen to God?
What fast from food, and what fast from sin, will I keep until Christmas?
pm.resp: Lord, wake us and make us ready.
interc: For the holy Church, that she may keep this fast with faith and prepare a worthy dwelling for the Lord.
For our families, that the Nombu may bring more prayer, peace and charity into our homes.
For those who are addicted to alcohol, drugs or screens, that the Lord may set them free.
For couples who long for a child, like Zechariah and Elizabeth, that they may know God's tenderness.
For the poor, that our fasting may become food for them.
pm.close: Lord God, you heard the prayer of Zechariah and made his silence fruitful. Bless our fast, purify our hearts and make us ready to welcome your Son with joy at Christmas. Amen.

illus: A schoolteacher in Thrissur decided one Nombu to keep the television off in the evenings. The first week the children complained. By the third week they were telling Bible stories at the dinner table and the family rosary had become the best part of the day. The fast had made room.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today our Church begins the twenty-five-day fast before Christmas, the Nombu that our ancestors kept with great seriousness. In many Kerala homes this fast still means no meat, simpler meals, more prayer and more almsgiving. But why do we fast before a feast? Because a great feast needs a prepared heart.

St Paul gives us the reason: you know what time it is; now is the moment to wake from sleep; salvation is nearer to us now than when we became believers; the night is far gone, the day is near (Romans 13:11–12). Christian life is a waking up. We can spend years half asleep: going through religious customs without noticing the Lord who comes.

Paul is very practical about what waking up means. Let us lay aside the works of darkness: not in drunkenness, not in quarrelling and jealousy. Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 13:13–14). The fast from food is meant to strengthen a deeper fast: from sin, from anger at home, from the bottle, from the phone that steals our evenings.

In the Gospel the angel Gabriel tells the old priest Zechariah that his long prayer has been heard: Elizabeth will bear a son. But Zechariah asks: how will I know this? I am old. And because he does not believe, he becomes unable to speak until the promise is fulfilled (Luke 1:18–20).

Zechariah's silence was a correction, but also a gift. For nine months he could not talk; he could only listen, watch and pray. When his son was born, his first words were not complaints but the great song of praise, the Benedictus. Silence prepared his heart to sing.

This Nombu, let us include some silence. Less noise, less screen, less gossip. More time in the church, more family prayer, more reading of the Gospel. Then, like Zechariah, we will have a song ready when Christmas comes.

Let us make three simple resolutions today: a fast from one food, a fast from one sin, and a daily act of charity. And let us ask Mary, who carried the Word in silence, to help us keep this fast with joy. Amen.
kids: Children, the fast before Christmas is like waking up early to get ready for a big feast. Give up one small thing for Jesus this month!

intro: Theme: “Wake up, and be silent before the Word.”
Paul calls us to wake; Zechariah's doubt becomes a fruitful silence.

sub: Malachi promised a messenger before the Lord.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
The angel replied, “I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.”
points.apply: Listen today for a message God may be sending.

sub: Silence becomes his school of faith.
q: Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?
Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know that this is so? For I am an old man, and my wife is getting on in years.”
